sources.label: About
sources.content: I work at the intersection of journalism, design, and governance research — with a stubborn habit of shipping. I report on tech policy and AI for outlets, sketch product systems for early-stage teams, and lead research projects on platform accountability. Currently focused on building tools that turn personal narrative into legible interfaces. I care about craft, plain language, and the moment a complicated idea suddenly clicks for someone.

sources.label: Work history (with numbers)
sources.content:
IBM (2020–2022) — Product designer on the Watson AI team. Shipped the redesigned Watson Assistant onboarding flow that reduced first-task drop-off by 38% and lifted weekly active developers by 22%. Owned design for an internal classifier-eval tool used by 600+ AI engineers across 14 countries.

Preface (2022–2024) — Design lead, then head of product. Grew weekly active learners from 4k to 120k in 18 months. Closed a $4.2M seed round (led by Sequoia) on the strength of the retention curve. Shipped the curriculum-builder that 3.5k educators now use to assemble their own coding lessons. NPS climbed from 41 → 67 across the period.

Freelance journalism — bylines at TechCrunch, Wired, Rest of World, MIT Tech Review. ~40 published features over 3 years on AI policy, platform accountability, and the politics of defaults.

Governance research — 2 years at NYU Information Law Institute. Co-authored 3 published papers on platform liability.

post 3: 'i keep a list of papers, products, and people i return to. the through-line, when i look back, is always: who took the time to make it legible?'

sources.label: Origin
sources.content: Started as a journalism student at NYU in 2017, covering NYC tech for the school paper. Got obsessed with how product decisions become policy. Took a sharp turn into product design after a long winter rebuilding the school paper's website by hand — realized I cared more about the artifact than the article. From 2019 onward, every job has been about that intersection: design that reads like reporting, and reporting that builds like design.

sources.label: How I work
sources.content: I write before I design — short specs, plain language. Pair on every meaningful design decision. Default to small, confident teams over big ones. Ship a v1 in a week, polish in public, treat the artifact as the spec. Strong opinions, loosely held. Allergic to performative process. Read papers in the morning, build in the afternoon, write at night.
